author: AI Editorial Team (Esi)
key_learning_objective: Teach the daily-weight parameter that warrants notifying the provider.
question_stem: A nurse is teaching a client with heart failure about daily weight monitoring. Which statement indicates correct understanding?

options.A: "I will call my provider if I gain 2 to 3 pounds in a single day."
options.B: "I should weigh myself only when I feel short of breath."
options.C: "A weight loss of 1 pound each day is a warning sign."
options.D: "I will weigh myself after dinner each evening."

rationales.A: Correct. A rapid gain of 2-3 lb (0.9-1.4 kg) in 24 hours, or ~5 lb in a week, signals fluid retention and worsening heart failure and should be reported.
rationales.B: Weight should be measured daily, not only when symptomatic, to catch fluid retention early.
rationales.C: Gradual weight loss with therapy is expected; sudden gain is the warning sign.
rationales.D: Weigh at the same time each day, ideally in the morning after voiding, before eating, in similar clothing.

key_takeaway: Same time, same scale, every morning. Report 2-3 lb/day or 5 lb/week gain.
nclex_test_taking_tip: For self-management teaching, the best answer names a specific, actionable threshold.
memory_trick: 2-3 in a day, 5 in a week - make the call.
clinical_pearls: Sudden weight gain reflects fluid, not fat.
Standardize the weigh-in: AM, post-void, same clothing.
